diagnosis: HARD CAP: run_all_variations._run_one wraps every orchestrator in subprocess.run(timeout=60*60) = 3600s. Line 54. Not configurable by CLI.
ADHOC SUITE IS 146 CASES vs static 59 (2.47x). Measured wall-clock throughput at --max-workers 2 is 28.8s per completed test (mean of tier-2-adhoc 29.5, tier-1-adhoc 28.7, tier0-adhoc 28.2).

ARITHMETIC: 146 cases x 28.8s = 4205s = 70.1 min needed, vs 3600s = 60.0 min allowed. Overshoot 605s (16.8%). Cases finishable before the axe: 3600/28.8 = 125 of 146 - and tier-2-adhoc actually produced 122. Prediction matches observation.
CONSEQUENCE: every one of the 8 adhoc jobs will be SIGKILLed at 3600s with rc=-1 and no aggregate-results.json, discarding ~124 scored outputs each. That silently voids 8 of 17 matrix cells (47%).

PER-TEST SERVICE TIME = wall x workers = 28.8 x 2 = 57.6s, matching the launching session's own '~60s/call' estimate. The session's throughput model was right; it simply never compared PER-JOB wall time against the 3600s per-job cap.

MISLEADING METRIC: aggregates.avg_latency_ms is NOT service time. orchestrator.py:811 computes it as time.time() - workers[tid]['start_time'] where all workers are queued at t=0, so it is queue-to-completion sojourn time. Proof: tier-1-static max_latency_ms=2060384 (2060s) vs job elapsed 2061s. Do not size timeouts from it.
STATIC JOBS ARE ALSO NEAR THE CLIFF: tier-2-static took 3366s, only 234s (6.5%) under the 3600s cap. A modest slowdown kills static jobs too.

TIERS 3/4/5 NOT YET REACHED AND AT HIGH RISK: system prompts are 398KB/474KB/552KB (~95K/116K/134K tokens) vs level-2's 5KB. Those 6 jobs face both far slower calls and possible context-window failures. None has started.

NO PARTIAL SALVAGE: orchestrator.py writes aggregate-results.json only after the whole scoring phase. subprocess.run timeout kills it mid-flight, so the 122 completed tier-2-adhoc outputs on disk are unscored and invisible to comparison.json.
recommended_fix: FIX 1 (smallest, unblocks now): make the per-job timeout proportional to suite size instead of a constant. Replace timeout=60*60 at run_all_variations.py:54 with a computed budget, e.g. timeout=max(3600, int(n_cases * 60 * 2 / max_workers * 1.5)), and expose it as --job-timeout. For 146 cases at 2 workers that yields ~6570s.

FIX 2 (better throughput): raise --max-workers. Minimum to fit 146 cases in 3600s is ceil(146*57.6/3600) = 3 workers; use --max-workers 4 for ~35 min with headroom. Keep --max-orchestrators 3 so total concurrency is 12.

FIX 3 (stop losing work): on subprocess.TimeoutExpired send SIGTERM and let orchestrator.py trap it to run the scoring phase over whatever *-output.txt files exist, emitting a partial aggregate with a 'partial': true flag. This alone would have salvaged 122/146 tier-2-adhoc results.
FIX 4 (symmetry): generate_adhoc_tests.py emits 146 cases against a 59-case static suite. Cap adhoc at 59 (--limit 59) so static and adhoc are directly comparable and both fit the budget.
FIX 5 (do not restart blindly): tier-1-static (96.6%) and tier-2-static (93.2%) are already complete and valid. Any rerun should skip jobs whose aggregate-results.json already exists.
